content:
Hi John

I can replicate your behaviour and think i can explain what's happening.

After you cleared the local messages and change the local folder size, your next step was pressing the load 100 more button. There's no mention of you synchronising the folder with the server before pressing the button.

When I replicate your steps I observe double the qty of messages downloaded compared to the local folder size value.

I believe pressing load more is doing 2 actions after local messages are cleared. 1. Performs an initial folder sync, downloads the first batch of emails (100). 2. Downloads the second batch of emails (100 more) requested because the load more button was pressed.

Can you try these steps instead. 1. Change the local folder size to your desired value (100) ++. 2. Change to a different folder, then switch back to inbox again. 3. Clear the local messages for inbox 4. Perform a pull down swipe gesture to sync the folder (loads first batch 100 emails) 5. Press the load 100 more button (only if you need an additional 100 emails).

++ I noticed the currently selected folder doesn't immediately pick up setting changes to local folder size until a different folder or account has been selected. The load x more messages button displays and uses the old values until after a change, hence step 2.

Unify

Toggling the Unify folder setting tells the app to display said folders content within the Unified Inbox. After electing to Unify sent and draft folders, it's the expected app behaviour to display their content within the Unified Inbox. Actions such as delete, move etc are performed on the original email.

The app doesn't yet have separate Unified Outbox, sent, draft, trash or Archive folders. That is a planned feature addition likely to arrive in a future update. See below for more info. https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/pull/11744
